pois.name: North wall of the upper canyon
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain (Ryan et al. 2009; value and slope read directly from this tile's grid this session): 541.9 m deep, on a locally steep flank of the upper canyon's north wall. Central-difference slope sampling over one grid cell (~50-60 m) gives roughly 18-19 deg here -- steep for this ~50 m grid, and the true wall relief (rock outcrops and ledges per MAFMC's habitat description) is almost certainly sharper than this coarse sampling can resolve.

pois.name: Coral-habitat ledge
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain (941.9 m deep, steep mid-canyon flank a little over 2.5 km from the wall POI) inside the Frank R. Lautenberg Deep Sea Coral Protection Area, which closes bottom-tending fishing gear across roughly 38,000 sq mi of Mid-Atlantic canyon and slope habitat including Hudson Canyon. In September 2025 a NOAA/Ocean Exploration Trust expedition used ROV Global Explorer to survey Hudson Canyon's coral and sponge communities for the first time in years, live-streamed as part of the sanctuary-designation science effort. No public dataset from that cruise gives an exact coral colony position usable here, so this POI's precise coordinate is an invented stand-in for that habitat type on a real steep ledge; `reconstruction: true` because no coral model is rendered -- the field guide entry, not a placed prop, carries the biology.

pois.name: Upper canyon floor
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain: 1,220.1 m deep, on the canyon axis (thalweg) below the wall/coral cluster. About 4.9 km southeast of the wall POI.

pois.name: Deepest point in this survey
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain, this tile's single deepest cell: -1,682.59 m (matches data/tiles/hudson-canyon/meta.json min_m), at the tile's southeast (offshore) edge. Hudson Canyon itself continues much deeper -- published figures put its lower reaches at 2-2.5 miles (roughly 3,200-4,000 m) -- well beyond this ~52x56 km survey tile, which only covers the canyon's upper/middle reaches from the shelf break outward. Optional: a deliberate long transit from the required objectives, about 9.4 km southeast of the wall POI.

pois.name: Hudson Shelf Valley (drowned river channel)
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain, 126.5 m deep, on the diagonal transect this session traced from the tile's shallow northwest corner toward its deep southeast corner as an approximation of the Hudson Shelf Valley/canyon axis (the valley's own USGS-mapped centerline is not reproduced exactly; this point sits within it on the coarse ~50-60 m grid). About 26 km northwest of the wall POI -- optional long-range objective, not required. Confidence 'medium' because the exact USGS valley thalweg was not cross-checked point-by-point against this tile's grid.

pois.name: Canyon head, outer shelf edge
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain, this tile's shallowest cell: -67.86 m (matches meta.json max_m), at the tile's northwest corner near the outer continental shelf. Published sources place the true canyon head (where the Hudson Shelf Valley funnels onto the shelf break) a little further north and east, around 39.66-39.67 N / 72.47-72.48 W, just outside this tile's north edge -- so this point is this survey's closest real approach to the head, not the literal head coordinate. About 34 km northwest of the wall POI; optional, distant lore objective.
